pages.text: Deep inside the ground, the Earth feels warm. Vicky the volcano rests quietly above it.
A volcano is an opening in the Earth. It connects the hot inside to the land above.
Far below, rock melts from heat. Melted rock under the ground is called magma.
When magma reaches the surface, it is called lava. Lava flows slowly and cools over time.
Some volcanoes erupt often. Others stay quiet for a very long time.
As lava cools, it hardens into new rock. Volcanoes can slowly build new land.
People do not live very close when volcanoes are active. Safety is important.
Scientists watch volcanoes carefully. They study heat, movement, and gas.
Vicky reminds us: the Earth is alive inside, slowly changing the land we see.
At bedtime, we remember: volcanoes show Earth’s heat and help shape new land.
